title: Observability — Error Tracking, Performance Monitoring, and RUM

subChunks.title: Observability — Error Tracking, Performance Monitoring, and RUM
subChunks.hookHtml: A React application in production is a black box without observability. Users encounter errors you never see. Performance degrades for users in certain regions or on certain devices. Bundle regressions ship silently. Observability means instrumenting your application so you know when things go wrong, why they went wrong, and who was affected — before users report it.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Error tracking with Sentry

// main.tsx:
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/react';

Sentry.init({
  dsn: import.meta.env.VITE_SENTRY_DSN,
  environment: import.meta.env.MODE,
  tracesSampleRate: 0.1, // Sample 10% of transactions
  integrations: [
    new Sentry.BrowserTracing(), // Performance monitoring
  ],
});
// Sentry-aware ErrorBoundary:
const SentryErrorBoundary = Sentry.withErrorBoundary(AppContent, {
  fallback: <ErrorPage />,
  beforeCapture: (scope, error, componentStack) => {
    scope.setTag('component', 'AppContent');
  },
});

// Manual error capture:
try {
  await dangerousOperation();
} catch (error) {
  Sentry.captureException(error, {
    extra: { userId, questId },
    tags: { feature: 'quest-acceptance' },
  });
  throw error; // Re-throw for the ErrorBoundary
}

Performance monitoring — Core Web Vitals

// Measure Core Web Vitals:
import { onCLS, onFID, onLCP, onINP, onFCP, onTTFB } from 'web-vitals';

function sendToAnalytics({ name, value, id }) {
  // Send to your analytics endpoint:
  fetch('/api/vitals', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ name, value, id }),
    keepalive: true, // Survives page unload
  });
}

onCLS(sendToAnalytics);  // Cumulative Layout Shift
onFID(sendToAnalytics);  // First Input Delay
onLCP(sendToAnalytics);  // Largest Contentful Paint
onINP(sendToAnalytics);  // Interaction to Next Paint
onFCP(sendToAnalytics);  // First Contentful Paint
onTTFB(sendToAnalytics); // Time to First Byte

Bundle size monitoring

# bundlesize in CI — fail the build if bundle exceeds limits:
# package.json:
"bundlesize": [
  { "path": "./dist/assets/index-*.js", "maxSize": "100 kB" },
  { "path": "./dist/assets/vendor-*.js", "maxSize": "200 kB" }
]

# In CI:
npx bundlesize
# Fails the build if any limit is exceeded

Structured logging

// A logger that works in both browser and SSR:
const logger = {
  info: (message: string, context?: object) => {
    if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') {
      // In production, send to logging service:
      Sentry.addBreadcrumb({ category: 'info', message, data: context });
    } else {
      console.log(`[INFO] ${message}`, context);
    }
  },
  error: (message: string, error?: Error, context?: object) => {
    Sentry.captureException(error, { extra: { message, ...context } });
    console.error(`[ERROR] ${message}`, error, context);
  },
};

// Usage:
logger.info('Quest accepted', { questId, userId });
logger.error('Payment failed', error, { amount, currency });

Feature flag integration

// Feature flags allow gradual rollouts and instant kill switches:
import { useFlag } from '@growthbook/growthbook-react';

function QuestBoard() {
  const showNewQuestUi = useFlag('quest-board-v2');
  return showNewQuestUi ? <QuestBoardV2 /> : <QuestBoardV1 />;
}

// In Sentry, tag errors with the feature flag state:
Sentry.setTag('flag:quest-board-v2', showNewQuestUi.toString());

Vex: "The purpose of observability is not to collect data — it's to reduce the time between 'something is wrong' and 'I know what and why'. Error tracking without context (userId, action, feature flags) tells you that an error happened. With context, it tells you who experienced it, what they were doing, and whether the new feature you just shipped caused it."

storyBeats.text: A user submits a bug report. 'The quest board is broken.' No error message. No steps to reproduce. No browser. No context. The developer opens Sentry and finds 47 identical errors with full stack traces, user sessions, and feature flag states.

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: Observability means you know about problems before users report them. Sentry captures every unhandled error with the full context: who, what component, what they were doing, what feature flags were active. Core Web Vitals tell you if your latest deploy made the page slower for real users, not just in Lighthouse.

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: Bundle size monitoring in CI means a 300kb dependency never accidentally ships to production. A feature flag integration means when the new quest board has a bug, you can turn it off in 30 seconds without a deployment.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Instrument an application for production observability:

  • Set up Sentry initialization (mock the DSN) with BrowserTracing
  • Wrap the app in a Sentry-aware ErrorBoundary
  • Add a structured logger that sends to Sentry in production and console in development
  • Add web-vitals measurement that logs to the console (mock the analytics endpoint)

guidedPracticeTests.label: Error boundary renders fallback when child throws

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a complete observability setup: (1) Real Sentry integration (use a free Sentry account) with error boundaries, breadcrumbs, and user context. (2) A performance budget enforced in CI using bundlesize — set a 150kb limit on your main JS bundle and verify it fails when you import a large library. (3) A feature flag system using a simple localStorage-based implementation that: lets you toggle flags in DevTools console, makes the active flags visible in Sentry error context, and gracefully disables features with a kill switch.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain what 'observability' means for a React application in production — what are the three pillars (errors, performance, traces) and why is each important? Walk through how you'd use Sentry to diagnose a production error: what information does a good Sentry event include, and what makes it actionable? Then explain Core Web Vitals — what do LCP, CLS, and INP measure and why do they matter for users?

questions.prompt: A production error is reported. The Sentry event shows the error but no user context. How do you improve this?
options: Call Sentry.setUser({ id, email }) after login — Sentry attaches this to all subsequent events so you can see which users experienced each error
Add more console.error calls throughout the application
questions.answer: Call Sentry.setUser({ id, email }) after login — Sentry attaches this to all subsequent events so you can see which users experienced each error
questions.explanation: Sentry.setUser() sets a user context that persists across all events in the session. Every subsequent error, breadcrumb, and transaction includes the user's ID. This enables filtering errors by user, reaching out to affected users, and understanding whether an error affected 1 user or 10,000. Combine with Sentry.setTag() for feature flags and setExtra() for additional debugging context.

questions.prompt: Your Lighthouse score is 95 in CI but users report the page feels slow. What observability data would you check?
options: Real User Monitoring (RUM) data — Core Web Vitals from real devices/networks. Lab tests (Lighthouse) use ideal conditions; RUM shows 90th-percentile experience on slow phones and congested networks.
The Sentry error rate — slow performance and errors correlate
The CI build time — longer builds mean heavier bundles
The number of API calls per page load
questions.answer: Real User Monitoring (RUM) data — Core Web Vitals from real devices/networks. Lab tests (Lighthouse) use ideal conditions; RUM shows 90th-percentile experience on slow phones and congested networks.
questions.explanation: Lighthouse runs in a controlled lab environment on a fast machine with throttled connection. Real users have slower devices, varying network conditions, browser extensions, and different geographic latency. RUM data (from web-vitals, Sentry Performance, or Vercel Analytics) shows the 75th or 90th percentile LCP/CLS/INP for real users — often 2-5x worse than lab scores.
